instructions.task: Select fact_pattern, lookup, conceptual or skip for the strongest supported information need in the TARGET ARTICLE. Do not generate questions or answers.

input_structure.### TARGET ARTICLE: The article whose legal point the question must concern.
input_structure.### REFERENCED ARTICLES: Supplied same-act provisions cited by the target.
input_structure.### REFERENCED ARTICLES FROM OTHER ACTS: Supplied cited provisions from other acts, with exact Cite as keys.
input_structure.### REFERENCED ANNEXES: Supplied cited annexes, with exact Cite as keys.

instructions.metadata: Act, Location, titles, article numbers and language tags identify the regime and supplied version. Different-language versions are the same provision. Metadata alone is not answer evidence.
instructions.grounding: The target must supply the legal point. Its explicit references may complete or clarify the rule using supplied material, but must not become the question's independent subject. Require a sufficient contiguous evidence span read with its question and governing clause; no stitched or invented explanation. Missing references exclude only needs dependent on them.
selection: Assess the strongest naturally supported need for all three modes before choosing. Select on faithful usefulness and fit, not mode order, expected verifier scores, preferred frequencies or a fixed tie preference. One strong question is enough.

Choose fact_pattern when meaningful case particulars make direct application a natural need; choose lookup when the need is a precise point of law; choose conceptual when the evidence answers a substantive relationship about a problem, legal response or affected party. None is a residual option available only after another fails.

The same topic may support more than one mode. Do not route by interrogative word, sentence length, the presence of a number/definition or an available act identifier. Do not force a case or broaden an isolated datum merely to favor a persona.

Preserve obligations, permissions, discretion, exceptions, conditions, and EU versus national roles. Legislation establishes legal arrangements, not evidence of their implementation, effectiveness or real-world results. Ask why only if the source expressly supplies a rationale.

Every mode needs enough substantive context to identify the regime. Use supported time/version or territorial context when material, not an arbitrary mandatory year. Do not assume current law or confuse publication, adoption and application dates.

Conceptual situation, response and stakeholder framings have equal standing. Substantive Commission, agency or other institutional relationships can qualify; conceptual mode does not require a private-party protagonist. Preserve each mode's eligibility rules below.

Lookup and fact_pattern retain their existing exclusions: pure transposition; application/entry-into-force; addressees/binding-entirety; repeal; committee procedure; definitive collection; institutional review/report/evaluation; financial-interests/audit access; delegation; generic penalty clauses; data-protection cross-references. A mixed article may still contain a non-excluded rule. For conceptual, judge whether the provision supports an informative regulatory relationship rather than an isolated datum or generic boilerplate; a substantive institutional mechanism can qualify even where the other modes exclude that topic. Skip only when all three lack a qualifying need.

criteria.fact_pattern: A concrete case involving a private party or national authority handling a file. At least two meaningful particulars establish scope or conditions of an explicit rule, without revealing its consequence or naming the governing instrument. Ordinary category, condition, threshold or date matching qualifies; no difficult dispute is required. Do not invent decorative details to fill slots.
criteria.lookup: A direct request for one precise legal point: a definition, scope rule, obligation, condition, deadline, threshold, duty, consequence, competent body or procedure. A substantive regime anchor identifies the need. Two renderings differ only by the target instrument identifier; a client scenario is unnecessary.
criteria.conceptual: The searcher knows a regulated issue or activity, not the governing instrument. One bounded relationship asks about an explicitly stated problem/rationale, how a legal measure or process operates, or how a defined party is affected or assigned responsibilities. No hypothetical client case or act locator is needed. Connected facts can answer one intent; isolated data or definitions relabelled with how/why do not qualify. Stated aims do not establish mechanisms, implementation or success.
criteria.skip: No mode supports a substantive, informative, grounded need about the target. Pure transposition, general commencement/repeal, generic review or generic penalty boilerplate and missing indispensable substance may warrant skip. Use substantive content in mixed articles; do not exclude an institutional actor or a concrete regulatory mechanism solely because of its heading.
